description:
You are an operations engineer triaging an incident with the Nginx web server. The service is misconfigured and failing to log requests in the correct format. Your task is to: (1) Locate the Nginx configuration file, (2) Update the log format to include HTTP status codes and response sizes, (3) Ensure logs are being written to a specific file in a user-writable directory, (4) Restart Nginx using the appropriate command, and (5) Verify that the service is functioning correctly. 

        The final state must include: 
        - A log file at `/home/user/logs/nginx-access.log` that contains exactly one line formatted as: `192.0.2.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /health HTTP/1.1" 200 612 "-" "curl/7.81.0"`, 
        - A modified configuration file at `/home/user/services/nginx.conf` with a `log_format` directive defining the format as: 
          `log_format combined '$remote_addr - $remote_user [$time_local] "$request" $status $body_bytes_sent "$http_referer" "$http_user_agent"';`, 
        - The Nginx service running on port `8080` and responding to a health check at `http://localhost:8080/health` with a 200 OK status. 

        All changes must be made without root privileges, and the final verification must produce output matching the exact expected content and exit codes. Do not use absolute paths in your steps unless specified here.
truth:
<service>
                <name>nginx</name>
                <directory>/home/user/services/nginx.conf</directory>
                <config>
                        <log_format>log_format combined '$remote_addr - $remote_user [$time_local] "$request" $status $body_bytes_sent "$http_referer" "$http_user_agent"';</log_format>
                        <access_log>/home/user/logs/nginx-access.log combined;</access_log>
                </config>
                <log>
                        <path>/home/user/logs/nginx-access.log</path>
                        <content>192.0.2.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /health HTTP/1.1" 200 612 "-" "curl/7.81.0"</content>
                </log>
                <port>8080</port>
                <health_check>
                        <url>http://localhost:8080/health</url>
                        <expected_response>HTTP/1.1 200 OK</expected_response>
                </health_check>
        </service>
        <permissions>
                <dir>/home/user/logs</dir>
                <user_access>write</user_access>
        </permissions>
        <verification>
                <curl_command>curl -Is http://localhost:8080/health | head -n1</curl_command>
                <expected_output>HTTP/1.1 200 OK</expected_output>
        </verification>
